thread.title: Parents call for transparency as Lincoln Unified considers new middle school - NewsBreak
thread.title_full: Parents call for transparency as Lincoln Unified considers new middle school - NewsBreak

author: Josie Heart
title: Parents call for transparency as Lincoln Unified considers new middle school - NewsBreak
text:
By Josie Heart ,
3 hours ago
(FOX40.COM) — The Lincoln Unified School District in Stockton is holding a board meeting on Wednesday night to discuss the possibility of creating a new middle school.
District leaders said that this move comes in response to growing demand from parents.
But some families are raising concerns, worried that opening a new campus could lead to closures of existing schools.
Parents like Aimee Burns say rumors have been circulating at Don Riggio School, a TK-6th-grade campus, that it may be shut down to make room for a new middle school. Burns said the uncertainty has caused a lot of worry.
“That my children’s school would be closed. Children would be displaced,” said Burns.
District officials said those rumors are not true. Ahead of the meeting, district spokesperson Tyler Heberle said discussions are still in early stages and that no decisions or votes are taking place this week.
“There is interest in an additional campus for seventh and eighth graders specifically,” said Heberle. “There’s also interest for TK through eight campuses to continue.”
Lincoln Unified currently has 12 schools, but only one campus dedicated solely to seventh and eighth graders. The district says parents have increasingly expressed interest in having more specialized middle school options.
Heberle said the need for another middle school is not due to an increase in students, but because students are growing up and moving on to higher grades, with parents and the students expressing a desire for a more focused space.
Heberle clarified that conversations are focused on how to reconfigure existing resources, not on closing down any schools.
“We do not intend to close any school altogether. We are looking at ways to most likely reconfigure our existing educational offerings,” said Heberle. “We have an enrollment level to where there’s not a way to build a 13th campus, but there are certainly ways to move around what’s offered at what campus, what facility specifically.”
Burns and other parents are pushing for the district to improve communication, especially for families who speak languages other than English, and for parents to be able to understand what the upcoming board meetings are about.
“Don Riggio in particular had a seventh and eighth grade program that was removed a couple of years ago. Parents were really against this decision, and it happened anyway. So, reintroduce them back. We’re happy to have them back,” said Burns.
Wednesday night’s board meeting will take place at the Beverly Holt Boardroom located on 6225 Harrisburg Place at 7 p.m.
District leaders say parents and community members are encouraged to attend, sign up to speak, and share their thoughts or concerns.
Heberle says discussions will continue during another board meeting in December.
